People possess basic rights because they are human; government is instituted to secure those rights.

Which conclusion most accurately applies natural rights to this evidence?

generalfeedback.text: natural-rights theory treats basic rights as preexisting government, while constitutional law defines enforceable protections and lawful limits.

answer.text: Any preference asserted by a citizen automatically becomes a natural right.

MLA Standard: MLA.USG.FND.2

The 1689 document restricted the monarch and protected parliamentary rights, including limits on suspending laws without Parliament.

Which conclusion most accurately applies English Bill of Rights to this evidence?

generalfeedback.text: the English Bill of Rights limited monarchy and strengthened parliamentary and individual protections that influenced later American ideas.

answer.text: It declared American independence from Britain.

feedback.text: This choice overgeneralizes the evidence or treats a limited principle as unlimited. the English Bill of Rights limited monarchy and strengthened parliamentary and individual protections that influenced later American ideas.

answer.text: It reinforced the principle that rulers are subject to law and that representative institutions possess protected authority.

feedback.text: The answer is supported because the English Bill of Rights limited monarchy and strengthened parliamentary and individual protections that influenced later American ideas.

answer.text: It created complete religious equality in every English colony.

feedback.text: This choice confuses a related constitutional concept with the one the evidence directly tests. the English Bill of Rights limited monarchy and strengthened parliamentary and individual protections that influenced later American ideas.

answer.text: It replaced Parliament with direct popular voting.

MLA Standard: MLA.USG.FND.3

The Articles had no separate national executive or general national judiciary, and amendment required confirmation by every state legislature.

Which conclusion most accurately applies enforcement and amendment to this evidence?

generalfeedback.text: the absence of separate enforcement and judicial institutions, combined with unanimity for amendment, limited effective national action and reform.

answer.text: Federal courts routinely invalidated state laws under the Articles.

answer.text: A president could enforce laws but Congress could remove the president at will.

feedback.text: This choice confuses a related constitutional concept with the one the evidence directly tests. the absence of separate enforcement and judicial institutions, combined with unanimity for amendment, limited effective national action and reform.

answer.text: Amendments required only a simple majority of Congress.

feedback.text: This choice adds a conclusion that the source or scenario does not support. the absence of separate enforcement and judicial institutions, combined with unanimity for amendment, limited effective national action and reform.

answer.text: National decisions were difficult to execute and formal reform was exceptionally difficult.

feedback.text: The answer is supported because the absence of separate enforcement and judicial institutions, combined with unanimity for amendment, limited effective national action and reform.

MLA Standard: MLA.USG.FND.4

The President vetoes a bill, and Congress considers whether to override by supermajority.

Which conclusion most accurately applies checks and balances to this evidence?

generalfeedback.text: checks give institutions limited tools to restrain one another; neither veto nor override eliminates the other branch.

answer.text: The sequence is federalism because two levels of government disagree.

feedback.text: This choice overgeneralizes the evidence or treats a limited principle as unlimited. checks give institutions limited tools to restrain one another; neither veto nor override eliminates the other branch.

answer.text: The sequence is an individual right held by Congress.

feedback.text: This choice confuses a related constitutional concept with the one the evidence directly tests. checks give institutions limited tools to restrain one another; neither veto nor override eliminates the other branch.

answer.text: The sequence allows either branch to enact law alone.

feedback.text: This choice adds a conclusion that the source or scenario does not support. checks give institutions limited tools to restrain one another; neither veto nor override eliminates the other branch.

answer.text: The veto and override are reciprocal checks within a separated lawmaking process.

feedback.text: The answer is supported because checks give institutions limited tools to restrain one another; neither veto nor override eliminates the other branch.
